payload.headline: Meta bounces to 628.96 above its 200-day average; still waiting for 2027-01-27

summary.thesis: Sales are still growing fast, but margins and free cash flow fell sharply, and at 628.96 the price assumes a cash recovery the reports have not shown yet.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, and buy only at 475.85 or after the 2027-01-27 report shows cash flow recovering. Swing: no trade, because the bounce has run into resistance.
summary.act_at: Buy at 475.85; swing only on a close above 659.3

payload.happening: Meta rose 3.13% to 628.96. That puts it just above its 200-day average of 626.67 but still well below its 50-day average of 671.34, and the overall trend is still down. No news has come out since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand still looks strong. Sales over the past year (trailing twelve months, TTM) are 241.6B, up from 189.5B, and the gross margin is 81.03%. Growth is slowing, though: sales rose 26.07% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, against 33.08% two quarters ago. Margins and cash are where the business is changing. The operating margin (profit from operations as a share of sales) fell to 32.86% from 43.23%. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for investment) fell to 28.6B from 44.8B. That puts the free-cash-flow margin at only 11.86%. Research spending is 31.68% of revenue. Heavy spending on AI computing has been widely reported (general knowledge) and fits these numbers. The filings flag that profit per share is lagging sales and that last quarter missed forecasts by 29%. The balance sheet is not at risk: debt is 83.7B, cash on hand is 11.2B, available liquidity is 82.4B, and net cash is only -1.2B, a near-even position. Share count rose just 0.04% in a year, so owners are not being diluted. The reported $14.1M of insider selling outside pre-set plans is a sentiment and governance point. It does not change the business. What is at risk is how much cash each dollar of sales turns into. Demand is not at risk.

worth.text: The two valuation methods disagree because they start from different numbers. A DCF (discounted cash flow: today's value of future cash) starts from the shrunken 28.6B of free cash flow and a 9.9% discount rate. It gives 244.22 in the bear case, 379.4 in the base case and 517.42 in the bull case, all below the price. To justify the price, free cash flow would need to start growing at 37.5% a year. Even at 30% starting growth the value is only 477.73. If the operating margin fell to 24%, the value would drop to 245.02. Meta's own price-to-sales history starts from sales, which are still rising. On that measure the stock sits at the 37th percentile of its last five years, with a range of 475.85 to 707.21 to 881.21. Other measures look moderate: the stock trades at 21.5 times trailing earnings and 6.7 times sales, against a peer median of 6.0 times sales. Adjusted for growth, it is roughly in line with peers (1.02). The whole gap comes down to one question: will cash flow return to its old relationship with sales?
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the heavy spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Sales grew 27.53% over the past year and the gross margin is 81.03%, so demand for the core business is intact.
Price-to-sales is at only the 37th percentile of Meta's own five-year range, and the midpoint of that history is 707.21.
Growth-adjusted, the stock is priced about in line with AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT and NFLX (1.02), and it trades at 21.5 times trailing earnings.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, and every DCF value (top: 517.42) is below the price.
The operating margin dropped to 32.86% from 43.23%, and last quarter missed forecasts by 29%.
The price needs 37.5% starting cash-flow growth, and a fall to a 24% operating margin would cut the value to 245.02.

levels.what: Bottom of the lower support zone (592.87–607.98). A close below it would mean today's bounce failed and the downtrend resumed.
The DCF bull value. Below it, the price no longer sits above every cash-flow estimate.
Buy level. It is the low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 477.73 value at 30% growth, so buying here does not depend on a full margin recovery.

longterm.why: At 628.96 the price is above every DCF value, the business is graded C, and free cash flow is shrinking. Buying now would mean paying in advance for a recovery that has not shown up yet.

swing.why: The close did clear the 200-day average of 626.67, but resistance starts at 644.84, less than one average daily move (ATR) of 25.45 away. The trend is still down and the 20-day average of 615.49 is falling. No trade until a close above 659.3.

decision.timing: Options price a 9.5% move by Dec 18 and an 18.3% move by Feb 19, a window that includes the 2027-01-27 report. That report settles the cash-flow question, so there is no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows the operating margin moving back toward 43.23% and free cash flow rising above 28.6B. That would support buying above 475.85, toward the 707.21 mid of own history.
A close above the 50-day average of 671.34, which also clears the 661.65–674.42 resistance zone, would end the lower-highs pattern and allow a swing entry.
A close below 592.87, or an operating margin moving toward 24% (value 245.02), would push the buy level down to the DCF values instead of 475.85.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait long-term, because free cash flow is still 28.6B against 44.8B a year earlier. The close above the 200-day average (626.67) that the last swing note set as its condition did come, but resistance at 644.84 is less than one ATR (25.45) away, so the swing condition moves up to a close above 659.3.
